key_insight: Domain-specific biomedical embeddings, especially BioBERT, improved detection of dosing-error risk in clinical trial protocols compared with a ClinicalBERT baseline.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help flag higher-risk protocols earlier, supporting safer trial review and monitoring.
method: Encoded clinical trial text with transformer models (ClinicalBERT, PubMedBERT, BioBERT, MedCPT).
Combined text embeddings with categorical metadata.
Compared classical ML and neural models using ROC-AUC to predict dosing error.
evidence_signal: BioBERT achieved an ROC-AUC of 0.794 under logistic regression, while the strongest models reached 0.821 to 0.853 for dosage-error prediction.
watch_item: Results come from model benchmarking on protocol text, so real-world use would need external validation and careful review for false alarms and dataset shift.
paper_title: CaresAI at CT-DEB26: Detecting Dosing Errors In Clinical Trials Using Domain-Specific Transformer Embeddings and Classification Models
